channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Over 200 kg of Drugs Seized in Kazakhstan; Woman Traveled from Almaty to Distribute
item.description: Kazakhstan seized over 200 kg of drugs, including marijuana, synthetics, and hashish, in the first ten days of November. Police arrested a woman in Pavlodar who had traveled from Almaty to distribute drugs, along with other suspects in various regions.

item.title: Astana to Host World Anti-Doping Agency Executive Meetings for First Time in Central Asia
item.description: Astana will become the first city in Central Asia to host meetings of the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) from November 22-27. Key WADA bodies, including the Governing Board and Executive Committee, will convene to discuss the World Anti-Doping Code and international cooperation. This marks a significant event for the region's sports governance.

item.title: GPS Tracker Fitted to Rare Lynx in Almaty Region for Scientific Study
item.description: A rare Turkestan lynx, listed in the Red Book, has been fitted with a GPS collar for the first time in Kazakhstan's Almaty region. Named Karasha, the predator will now be monitored via satellite, allowing scientists to study its life in its natural habitat.

item.title: Stigma and Misconceptions Prevent Afghans from Seeking Mental Health Treatment
item.description: Specialists in Afghanistan report that stigma, fear of being labeled "crazy," and misconceptions about psychiatric medication prevent many individuals from seeking or continuing mental health treatment. Families sometimes attribute problems to weak faith or witchcraft, opting for religious healers over doctors, which can worsen conditions.

item.title: Doctors Warn of Serious Health Consequences from Antibiotic Misuse
item.description: Doctors are warning about the increasing arbitrary use of medicines, especially antibiotics, stating that improper use leads to serious health consequences and increased microbial resistance. Factors include taking antibiotics without a prescription, choosing the wrong type, and ignoring side effects, often due to cost concerns for examinations and doctor visits.

item.title: Drought and Conflict Push Haiti Towards Widespread Famine, UN Warns
item.description: Approximately 6 million people in Haiti face food insecurity, with nearly 2 million experiencing severe hunger. The UN attributes the worsening situation to armed violence, rising food prices, and drought. Without intervention, over half the population could face famine by mid-2027.

item.title: Armenian PM Announces 'Trump Route' Project for International Peace and Prosperity
item.description: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan announced the launch of the 'Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity' (TRIPP) project. A key component involves connecting Armenia's electricity grid with Turkey and Azerbaijan, alongside existing links to Iran and Georgia. The project also includes infrastructure for road, rail, and energy transit.

item.title: Former Uzbek Official Sought Internationally Extradited from Turkey
item.description: A former state employee, who was internationally wanted, has been returned to Uzbekistan from Turkey. The individual is accused of embezzling state funds and forging documents during their tenure as an official at the Khorezm regional Employment Assistance department.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Banking System Undergoing Changes: Increased Client Freedom and New Security Rules
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank is implementing changes to its banking system, offering more client freedom in salary account selection and tightening P2P transfer security with biometric identification. Banks will be responsible for fraudulent operations. The system aims for greater client freedom and bank responsibility, with a focus on security and service quality.

item.title: Trump Warns of US Bankruptcy Risk if Debt Limit Issue Unresolved
item.description: Former US President Donald Trump stated that the country could face bankruptcy if the issue of the national debt ceiling is not resolved. He proposed completely removing the legal procedure for setting the debt limit, citing it as a significant risk to the economy.

item.title: Power line connecting Uzbekistan and Tajikistan restored after outage
item.description: An outage on the 500 kV "L-503" power line, connecting Uzbekistan's "Sirdaryo" thermal power station and "Uzbekistan" substation via Tajikistan, has been fully repaired. The line was restored on November 22. The incident occurred on November 19 due to adverse weather conditions and difficult terrain, causing temporary power restrictions in parts of the Fergana Valley.

item.title: Iran's IRGC claims attack on US Patriot radars in Bahrain
item.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claims to have attacked two US Patriot air defence radars at bases in Bahrain. The IRGC announced this claim on Sunday, November 22. Bahrain has condemned alleged Iranian drone attacks on its territory, stating they hit a civilian facility and caused damage. The US military has not confirmed or denied the claim.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to liquidate UK-sanctioned company 'Processing.kg'
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has decided to liquidate OAO 'Processing.kg', a company that received 200 million soms in state capital increase. The company and its head were sanctioned by the UK a month prior. The Ministry of Finance, as the sole shareholder, approved the liquidation on November 16, 2026.

item.title: Power outage resolved after electricity pylon collapse on L-503 line
item.description: The power outage caused by the collapse of an electricity pylon on the L-503 transmission line, connecting the "Sirdaryo" thermal power plant and the "Uzbekistan" substation, has been fully resolved. Electricity transmission through the line, which passes through Tajikistan, has been restored.

item.title: Zelensky Proposes Evacuating 15 Settlements, Citing Oleshki Example
item.description: Ukrainian President Zelensky has proposed evacuating 15 settlements, using Oleshki as an example. The proposal includes locations in the Kherson and Zaporizhzhia regions, with the list potentially expanding based on population and conditions.

item.title: Taliban Report Three Armed Robbers Killed in Kabul
item.description: The Taliban authorities have reported that three armed robbers were killed in Kabul. Further details regarding the incident, the identities of the individuals, or the circumstances of their deaths were not provided in the source text.

item.title: Houthis Deny Threatening Mecca, Claim Operations Target Military Objectives
item.description: Yemen's Houthi military spokesperson, Yahya Saree, denied any threat to the holy city of Mecca, stating their operations exclusively target military objectives. He called Saudi Arabia's security warning for Mecca a "major fabrication." Saree asserted that Houthi actions are directed at oil facilities and military bases, not civilian or religious sites.

item.title: New Hippodrome Construction Begins in Sokuluk, Kyrgyzstan
item.description: A project to build a National Equestrian Sports Complex is underway in Sokuluk, Kyrgyzstan. The complex will feature a 10,000-seat hippodrome for races and a 25,000-seat arena for Kok Boru. The Bishkek mayor's office announced the plans, which include modern facilities and infrastructure on a 114-hectare site.

item.title: Bahrain Urges UN Security Council to Halt Iran's Attacks
item.description: Bahrain's Ministry of Foreign Affairs condemned Iran's recent airstrikes on its territory, calling them a direct threat to civilians and a violation of sovereignty. Bahrain urged the UN Security Council to take decisive measures to stop the attacks, which it deems a violation of the UN Charter and international law.

item.title: Teenager Beaten by High Schoolers in Kazakhstan Remains in Coma
item.description: A 14-year-old boy in Kazakhstan's Zhambyl region, severely beaten by high school students, is still in a coma. Doctors report his condition is extremely serious, though he has started breathing independently. The incident occurred in late October, and investigators have identified a suspect.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Head of Gardening Cooperative Arrested for Extorting $100,000
item.description: The head of a gardening cooperative and an alleged accomplice have been arrested in Kyrgyzstan's Chuy region for extorting $100,000 from entrepreneurs. They are accused of threatening business activities if the money was not paid.

item.title: Drunk Driver Evades Police, Collides with Patrol Car in Abai Region
item.description: In the Urzhar district of Abai region, a 62-year-old driver refused to stop for police and attempted to flee. During the pursuit, the driver collided with a patrol car. A sobriety test confirmed the driver was intoxicated. Police have forwarded materials for two offenses to court.

item.title: Turkish Foreign Minister Urges Iran-US Agreement, Regional Conflict Resolution
item.description: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan emphasized diplomatic efforts towards an Iran-US agreement, stating it's crucial for easing global economic pressures and potentially containing financial crises. He also called for regional countries to resolve their differences directly, without external actors, while noting ongoing, albeit stalled, communications regarding the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Kazakh Doctors Collaborate with International Professors on Complex Surgeries
item.description: An international educational course concluded at the Kazakh Research Institute of Oncology and Radiology in Almaty, gathering over 500 local and foreign doctors. Leading specialists shared expertise on complex surgeries, modern diagnostics, and cancer treatment. A live surgery demonstration for stomach cancer was broadcast to regional oncologists.

item.title: Saudi Parliament Speaker Abdullah Al Sheikh Arrives in Kyrgyzstan for Official Visit
item.description: Abdullah Al Sheikh, Speaker of the Shura Council of Saudi Arabia, arrived in Kyrgyzstan on November 22 for an official visit. He is scheduled to hold talks with the Speaker of the Jogorku Kenesh, Marlen Mamataliev. The visit aims to strengthen bilateral relations, expand cooperation, and enhance inter-parliamentary contacts between the two countries.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Faces Billion-Dollar Debt and Governance Challenges, Economy Grows
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's GDP grew 10.5% in Jan-Oct 2026, reaching 1.87 trillion soms. Industrial output rose 5.2%, with annual inflation at 11.1% in October. The EBRD reported a decline in governance quality to 4.34 points, citing press freedom and AML/CFT concerns, though economic stability improved.

item.title: Kazakh Rescuers Showcase New Equipment to Clear Fire Truck Access
item.description: Rescuers in Almaty and Astana demonstrated new equipment designed to move illegally parked cars blocking access for fire trucks. The specialized tools allow emergency services to quickly clear pathways for fire engines and rescue operations, ensuring faster response times.

item.title: Panjshir Youth Face Discrimination in NGO Job Recruitment, Study Finds
item.description: A study by the Panjshir Studies Centre reveals that young people from Panjshir face discrimination in recruitment for NGOs working with international organizations. Out of over 300 employees in Panjshir, only 60 are local residents, with most management positions held by non-Panjshiris. The report highlights preferential hiring and limited access to opportunities for local youth.

item.title: Uzbekistan-Kazakhstan Border Truck Congestion Due to Increased Freight Traffic, Customs Says
item.description: Uzbekistan's Customs Committee commented on social media videos showing truck congestion at the border with Kazakhstan. The committee stated that border crossing points are operating normally. However, data from the Turkestan region shows 100 trucks queued at the 'B. Konysbayev' crossing on November 20. The daily flow of trucks has increased significantly, with transit cargo being the main component.

item.title: Uzbekistan and US Discuss Strengthening Strategic Partnership
item.description: A roundtable on "New Uzbekistan and Uzbek-American Strategic Ties" was held in Washington. The event, hosted by the Hudson Institute, included Uzbek delegation members and US experts. Discussions focused on expanding industrial, technological, and regional security cooperation, with a noted increase in US interest in Central Asia.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Train Air Traffic Controllers Using American Programs
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to open a branch of the American Kent State University to train air traffic controllers, pilots, and aviation engineers. An agreement was reached following a meeting between Kazakhstan's Ministry of Transport and the university. The educational center will also serve other Central Asian countries.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkey Enter New Phase of Economic Partnership
item.description: Uzbekistan and Turkey are strengthening their economic ties, with Turkey being a major trade partner. Trade turnover has grown significantly, exceeding $3 billion by 2025. Turkey's expertise in industry, construction, and textiles, combined with Uzbekistan's resources, forms a basis for mutual benefit.

item.title: New 550 MW thermal power plant in Jizzakh region connected to grid
item.description: A new 550 MW thermal power plant in Uzbekistan's Jizzakh region, built by Turkey's Cengiz Enerji, has begun supplying electricity to the national grid. The plant uses combined cycle gas turbines and is expected to generate 4.4 billion kWh annually, saving 500 million cubic meters of natural gas. The project cost $500 million.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Host Branch of American University for Aviation Specialists
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to open a branch of the American Kent State University, which trains aviation specialists. This new educational center could become a regional hub for pilots, air traffic controllers, and technical staff in Central Asia. The agreement was reached during a meeting between Kazakh officials and the university delegation.

item.title: Afghanistan and Kenya Discuss Expanding Trade and Mining Cooperation
item.description: Afghanistan's Minister of Industry and Commerce, Nooruddin Azizi, met with Kenya's Minister of Mining, Hassan Ali Joho, on the sidelines of the Tanzania Investment Conference. They discussed expanding trade, economic cooperation, and potential collaboration in mining, mineral processing, and agricultural production. Both sides expressed interest in increasing trade exchanges and improving market access for their respective products.

item.title: Experts Discuss China-US-Russia Summit, Rejecting 'Yalta 2.0' Comparison
item.description: Experts discussed a trilateral meeting between China, the US, and Russia in Shenzhen, rejecting comparisons to the 'Yalta Conference 2.0'. They analyzed potential long-term consequences of the final declaration and the future of the trilateral format, concluding that the meeting did not resemble the historical Yalta conference's division of spheres of influence.

item.title: UN Chief Warns Rising Poverty and Conflicts Threaten Children's Future
item.description: UN Secretary-General António Guterres warned that increasing child poverty, armed conflicts, and climate shocks are jeopardizing children's futures. He called for stronger action to protect children's rights and ensure access to essential services like healthcare and education, emphasizing the need for sustained investment and commitment to their well-being and development.

item.title: Iran Confirms Qatari Delegation Visited Tehran for Nuclear Talks
item.description: Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi confirmed a Qatari delegation visited Tehran to discuss ending the war with the US. He stated that Iran is in contact with mediators, including Qatar, to explore diplomatic opportunities.

item.title: Video Surfaces of Azerbaijan Airlines Plane Crash Near Aktau
item.description: A full video of an Embraer 190 aircraft from Azerbaijan Airlines, which crashed near Aktau, has circulated on social media. The footage shows the plane flying at a low altitude before crashing and catching fire. Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev pledged full efforts to investigate the incident.

item.title: UK Government Concerned Over Potential New US Military Action Against Iran
item.description: The UK government and senior officials are discussing the possibility of renewed large-scale US military strikes against Iran. Potential Iranian retaliation is also a cause for concern for high-ranking British officials.
